newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Moldova replaces minister accused of corruption.
newsitem.headline: Moldova replaces minister accused of corruption.

text.p: Moldovan Privatisation Minister Ceslav Ciobanu was dismissed on Tuesday after being accused of corruption by parliament.
President Petru Lucinschi named economist Iurie Badir, one of the authors of Moldova's voucher mass privatisation scheme, to replace him.

Parliament called for Ciobanu's dismissal last month after a parliamentary committee charged that he favoured the illegal sale of a state sanatorium to an organisation whose founders included his wife.
He denied the charge but offered his resignation.
"Parliament's accusation is not objective," Ciobanu told a news conference on Tuesday, warning that quarrels over privatisation could block World Bank borrowing.
Two hours later the decree from Lucinschi accepting his resignation and appointing Badir was published by the presidential press service.
Badir, a member of the state audit office, previously headed the privatisation programme in the capital, Chisinau.
At the news conference Ciobanu accused parliament of impeding the adoption of the 1997-1998 privatisation programme, saying the delay could threaten a 35-million World Bank loan.
"Conservative forces have united against reforms and privatisation", Ciobanu said.

"Moldova is late with presenting a set of pro-reform decisions to the World Bank board. Its meeting, which has to consider a $35 million loan to Moldova in late June, might be cancelled," Ciobanu said.
On June 26, the World Bank board will consider a structural adjustment loan amounting to $100 million.
The first $35-million tranche could be issued in July if Moldova meets various conditions including passing the privatisation programme.
Moldova's 1994-6 mass privatisation programme, carried out by issuing free vouchers to the population, was praised by international organisations.
But in the second half of last year the World Bank and International Monetary Fund expressed concern over a slowdown in reforms, in particular cash privatisation.
The World Bank representative to Moldova declined to comment on Ciobanu's dismissal.
